questions.prompt: What does 70% calibration mean across many similar forecasts?
questions.answer: Approximately 70% of events assigned that probability occur.
questions.feedback: Check the definition and explain it in your own words before retrying.

questions.prompt: What is the Brier loss for p=0.8 and outcome 0?
questions.feedback: Check the distinction or calculation against the worked case; correct the first unsupported step.

questions.answer: A score needs context to assess whether a forecast adds value.
questions.feedback: State a concrete implication or limitation and retry without notes.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Computes a Brier score, interprets calibration cautiously and compares a fixed baseline.
scoring.transfer: Complete a forecast journal with at least ten synthetic resolved events and a fixed baseline; report scores and bin counts. Extend using low-stakes real forecasts only when independently resolvable.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; quiz score alone is insufficient.
